_comment: These are APPROXIMATIONS, not licensed data. Figures are public manufacturer
specs rounded to what the sim can actually express, and the names are here so
the handling targets are legible — ship them under original names.
UNITS: torque Nm at the crank, mass kg, dims meters (feet in the comment),
track = full axle width, comHeight = center of mass above ground (the new
IPhysicsWorld::addBox comOffset param; rollover threshold ~ atan(halfTrack /
WHY comHeight MATTERS MOST: it is the single parameter that separates these
cars in feel. The Plaid's floor battery is why it corners flat; the Cobra's
iron blower motor sitting high is why it leans. Torque alone will not do it.
gripScale multiplies Jolt's default (economy) tyre curve — 1.0 is a road
tyre, ~1.7 the current sports baseline, ~2.1 a modern performance compound.

cars.name: CTR
cars.dimsFeet: 5.5 W x 3.3 H x 12.8 L (halfExtents[0] is the GLB's TRUE half-width; buildPhysics multiplies it by the kBodyWiden 1.18 stance factor to reach the shipped 1.07 collision half-width)
cars.note: The 993-shaped baseline. comHeight lowered from 0.76 on 2026-08-14 to stop it rolling. RECONCILED 2026-08-16 against what is actually driven. Three figures here had drifted from app/vehicle.cpp: torque 700 -> 800 and redline 6500 -> 7500 (Tim re-tuned this engine by ear on 2026-08-15 — 'rev faster and pull HARD', titanium valve retainers), and mass 1300 -> 1083.2 (the value buildPhysics really creates the chassis body with). This matters because the JSON layer OVERRIDES the built-in table: unreconciled, the first successful load of this file would have quietly undone a day of tuning and added 217 kg to the hero car, with nothing reporting it. --test-carspec C11/C12 now hold the two sources together.

cars.name: Model S Plaid-alike
cars.note: Heaviest and lowest. Full torque from 0 rpm, ONE ratio, no shift points. AWD launch is why it beats the others off the line despite the mass. Floor-mounted battery = the flattest cornering in the roster.

cars.name: NSX Type S-alike
cars.note: Mid-engine, so the lowest comHeight and the widest track relative to length — the corner-carver of the three. Electric front axle fills torque below boost; approximate with a flat low-rpm floor rather than a turbo dip.

cars.name: '03 Cobra-alike (Terminator)
cars.note: The character car. Highest comHeight (tall iron blower motor up front), narrowest track for its mass, and the lowest grip — it should feel like it wants to step out and roll onto its outside wheel. Do NOT sanitise this one; the contrast against the Plaid is the point.
